items.title: Delhi High Court refuses urgent hearing in Youth Congress petition for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday refused to allow urgent listing of a petition filed by Indian Youth Congress (IYC) challenging the Delhi Police' refusal to permit them to hold a demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar. The plea filed by IYC national president Uday Bhanu Chib was mentioned before acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambre by Senior Advocate Sanjoy Ghose . Ghose said that he had mentioned the matter yesterday too and the Court had granted him liberty to mention the matter today if it is not listed. "What is the urgency? We will hear it on Monday," Justice Sambre said. Chib has challenged the Delhi Police’s order of October 1 rejecting their application. According to the plea, the IYC had applied on September 25 seeking permission to hold a peaceful demonstration involving around 100-150 people. The organisation said it had undertaken to comply with all lawful conditions relating to security, traffic management, discipline and maintenance of public order. items.title: Delhi’s Detention Day: Protesters picked up, journalists detained
items.summary: People picked up from the streets. Journalists detained. Reporting phones seized. Delhi’s October 10 protest became a day of sweeping detentions. Ahead of the protest demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and opposing SIR, access to Jantar Mantar was choked by layers of barricades and heavy police deployment. People travelling towards Delhi reported being detained on trains, while buses were diverted and students warned against attending. On the ground, Newslaundry reporters were detained and their work phones seized. They have since been released, but other journalists and YouTubers remained in detention at the time of this update. What does the right to protest mean if you cannot reach the protest site? And how do journalists show you what is happening when they, too, are put on detention buses? Watch our ground reports from a day of sweeping police action in the capital. We will continue to report. Newslaundry has no advertisers to please and no one to answer to but you, the reader. items.title: Three Newslaundry reporters detained by Delhi Police, since released
items.summary: Delhi Police detained our reporters Ashwine, Astha and Anmol and intern Anshu while they were covering the October 10 protest. They have since been released and are back reporting. Police seized Anmol’s and Anshu’s phones, while Ashwine was pushed and his phone snatched; all three phones were official Newslaundry devices used for reporting. When the journalists identified themselves as members of the media, they were reportedly told, “Koi media nahin hai.” Around 30 people, including protesters and journalists, were put into a single bus and taken to Chhatrasal Stadium in north Delhi. Our reporters identified Inspector Dhan Singh Malik as the officer who snatched the phones. Scroll’s Ayush Tiwari also detained Scroll ’s investigative reporter Ayush Tiwari was detained by Delhi Police near ITO, the outlet’s executive editor Supriya Sharma said in a post on X. “My colleague, one of India’s best investigative reporters, Ayush Tiwari @sighyush , has been detained by Delhi Police near ITO,” Sharma wrote. “He was not even at Jantar Mantar. He had his press card prominently displayed. He told the police many times he was a journalist. Despite that he was bundled into a van and taken away.

items.title: Delhi Police to decide in 15 days whether to challenge Brij Bhushan's acquittal in sexual harassment case
items.summary: The Delhi Police told a sessions court on Friday that the decision as to whether it will file an appeal against the acquittal of former BJP MP and ex-chief of the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) Brij Bhushan in the sexual harassment case filed against him by women wrestlers is "under process". While the wrestlers have already challenged the trial court's acquittal verdict of August 3 , the State is yet to file its appeal. Advocate Manish Rawat appeared for the prosecution today and said that the decision is under process. He sought 15 days to inform the court about the prosecution's decision. Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh allowed the request. The Court also granted Brij Bhushan time till October 28 to file his reply to the appeal filed by wrestlers. Pertinently, the Court clarified that the case will be heard in-camera, which means the public and media will not have access to hearings anymore. The case pertains to sexual harassment allegations raised by six women wrestlers against Singh. Based on their complaints, the police had registered a first information report (FIR) against the MP. items.summary: दिल्ली की सड़कों पर आज पुलिस पूरी तरह धरपकड़ के मूड में नजर आई. प्रदर्शनकारियों से लेकर पत्रकारों तक सबको एक सिरे से उठाया गया. साथ ही रिपोर्टिंग के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाले फोन जब्त किए गए. इस तरह आज का दिन बड़े पैमाने पर हिरासत की कार्रवाई के नाम रहा. गौरतलब है कि मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफ़े की मांग और चुनाव आयोग की ओर से जारी विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण के विरोध में होने वाले प्रदर्शन से पहले जंतर-मंतर तक पहुंचने के रास्तों पर बैरिकेडिंग कर दी गई थी और भारी संख्या में पुलिस बल तैनात था. दिल्ली आ रहे लोगों ने ट्रेनों में हिरासत में लिए जाने की बात कही, वहीं बसों के रास्ते बदले गए और छात्रों को प्रदर्शन में शामिल न होने की चेतावनी दिए जाने की खबरें भी सामने आईं. मौके पर रिपोर्टिंग कर रहे न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री के पत्रकारों को भी हिरासत में लिया गया और उनके काम के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाले फोन जब्त कर लिए गए. घंटों बाद उन्हें रिहा किया गया, लेकिन इस अपडेट के समय तक दूसरे पत्रकार और यूट्यूबर्स हिरासत में थे. ऐसे में बड़ा सवाल यही है कि अगर आप प्रदर्शन स्थल तक पहुंच ही नहीं सकते, तो विरोध करने के अधिकार का क्या मतलब रह जाता है? और जब पत्रकारों को भी हिरासत में लेकर बसों में बैठा दिया जाए, तो वे आपको वहां की स्थिति कैसे दिखाएंगे? राजधानी में पुलिस की व्यापक कार्रवाई के दिन की हमारी ग्राउं
